body:
> * variables typed as `Array[MyEnum]` will output `enum="MyEnum[]"` instead of `enum="MyEnum"` (in addition to `type="int[]"`

I don't think it's a bug, it's just a weird format. We don't have a unified type system and FQTNs (fully qualified type names) yet, for enumerations both "real" (`int`) and "imaginary" are specified. Same for arrays.

Working around the "array" enum was easy enough, but I just noticed something related to point 3 (again, not about XML files, but the editor's help instead): you *can* have working links to enum values, but you have to omit the enum name, e.g. `[MyClass.MyEnum.VALUE]` doesn't work, but `[MyClass.VALUE]` [does work](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12513#issuecomment-2915265924) - but what if several enums in the class have values with the same names?

Edit: I opened a separate issue for this specific point: #106894.

Not a regression from 4.5

This xml is generated by both godot 4.4.1 and 4.5-beta1
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<class name="DocToolIssue" inherits="Node" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/godot/master/doc/class.xsd">
	<brief_description>
	</brief_description>
	<description>
	</description>
	<tutorials>
	</tutorials>
	<members>
		<member name="some_var" type="int[]" setter="" getter="" enum="DocToolIssue.MyEnum[]" default="[]">
			An array of [enum MyEnum] values. [constant MyEnum.FIRST_VALUE] means something, [constant MyEnum.SECOND_VALUE] means another thing.
		</member>
		<member name="another_var" type="int" setter="" getter="" enum="DocToolIssue.MyEnum" default="0">
			This one works properly.
		</member>
	</members>
	<constants>
		<constant name="FIRST_VALUE" value="0" enum="MyEnum">
			An enum value for [enum MyEnum].
		</constant>
		<constant name="SECOND_VALUE" value="1" enum="MyEnum">
			An enum value for [enum MyEnum].
		</constant>
	</constants>
</class>
```

Of the 3 issues listed here, 1 and 3 are already covered in different issues and 2 is possibly not really a bug but just weird formatting so shouldn't this really be more of a tracking issue? I agree that the `MyEnum[]` thing is weird but we'd need to have a spec for whether that's expected or not to call it a bug
